organization.summary: SEAL Intel is the threat intelligence arm of Security Alliance (SEAL). Its page states 300+ threat reports and 200K+ malicious domains blocked, with MetaMask, Phantom and WalletConnect named as partners (self-reported). Public outputs include the SEAL Radar publication, the lazarus.group records site and the lazarus-group-data repository. The proposal budgets USD 267,000 and says the Ethereum Foundation is only a prospective funder. Public team size: Not found in public sources.

claims.claim: SEAL Radar publishes threat research, incident analysis and operational statistics.
claims.method: Radar returns HTTP 200 and lists 55 posts. The weekly stats post dated 2026-10-27 reports 73 triaged incidents and 5,179 malicious domains collected. The figures are SEAL's own and were not rechecked.

claims.claim: A public Lazarus intelligence dataset exists.
claims.method: GitHub API: CC-BY-4.0 repository, created 2026-10-28, last push 2026-11-17, described as SEAL's open data behind lazarus.group. The lazarus.group site returns HTTP 200 and says it is maintained by the Security Alliance and searches 395 profiles and 974 indicators.

claims.claim: SEAL maintains public GitHub repositories and datasets.
claims.method: 47 public repositories. blocklists was pushed 2026-11-28 and seal-911 (341 stars) on 2026-11-22.

claims.claim: SEAL identifies about 5,000 to 10,000 malicious frontends weekly and integrates with MetaMask's eth-phishing-detect.
claims.method: The weekly stats post reports thousands of malicious domains collected per week. The blocklists repository is described as a mirror of lists maintained by SEAL. The eth-phishing-detect README does not mention SEAL, and the integration was not independently confirmed.

claims.claim: SEAL maintains more than 100 communication channels and hotlines.
claims.method: A statement in the proposal. No public list of channels was found.

claims.claim: SEAL Intel has published 300+ threat reports and blocked 200K+ malicious domains.
claims.method: The page states both figures. They are self-reported, and no independent count was found.

claims.claim: The proposed TAXII 2.1 and REST feeds, STIX 2.1 records and ISAC workflows exist.
claims.method: These are grant deliverables. The seal-intel-sdk repository is linked from the SEAL Intel page and was last pushed 2026-03-13. No public TAXII feed was found.
